title: DOE-UAP-D004, Los Alamos Conference on Aerial Phenomena, 1949
doc_notes: This document is a transcript of a 1949 conference held at Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory to discuss the nature of 'green fireballs' reported in the region, featuring input from scientists and military personnel.

incidents.summary: Green fireball observed near Starvation Peak, New Mexico, with horizontal trajectory and constant angular velocity.
incidents.quote: This fireball which I personally witnessed on the night of December 12, 1948, was not, in my opinion, a conventional meteor fall.

incidents.summary: Large green fireball observed over New Mexico and Western Texas, with no associated sound or ground impact.
incidents.quote: In the case of the January 30th fall, due to the fact that there had been a large number of military personnel alerted, we were able to obtain observations within a minute after the fall occurred

incidents.summary: Green fireball observed near Roswell, New Mexico, by five men near a steel smokestack, accompanied by a sound like a gasoline blowtorch.
incidents.quote: every one of them swore that they heard at the same time they were watching the green fireball go by, a noise like, say, a gasoline blowtorch.
